questions.prompt: In the Network panel, what does the "Transferred" value represent?

options.text: The uncompressed size of the resource on disk
The bytes actually sent over the wire, after compression
The number of requests to that origin

questions.explanation: Transferred is the over-the-wire byte count (after compression); Size is the uncompressed resource. A big gap means good compression, and "(from cache)" means it wasn't downloaded.

questions.prompt: The Network column that shows WHAT caused a request (so you can trace dependency chains) is the ____ column.
questions.explanation: The Initiator column shows what triggered each request — the HTML or another script — revealing request chains where one resource gates another.

questions.prompt: Which settings help you test a realistic first-visit mobile experience? Select all that apply.

options.text: Test on office fibre with the cache warm

questions.explanation: Disabling the cache simulates a new visitor, and network/CPU throttling mimics a mid-range phone. A warm cache on fast fibre hides the real first-visit cost.

questions.prompt: Order these per-request timing phases as they occur.
questions.explanation: A request queues, resolves DNS, connects (TCP+TLS), waits for the first byte (TTFB), then downloads the content. Setup phases only appear on the first request to an origin.

questions.prompt: Match each Network column to what it tells you.

pairs.right: The browser's fetch order for the request

questions.explanation: Status is the HTTP outcome, Initiator traces chains, Transferred is compressed bytes, and Priority controls ordering.

questions.prompt: Why turn on "Disable cache" when profiling a page?

options.text: To make the page load faster in the test
To simulate a first-time visitor with an empty cache, revealing the true download cost
To remove images from the page

questions.explanation: With the cache on, repeat visits show tiny "(from cache)" entries that hide the real cost new visitors pay. Disabling it forces a cold, first-visit load.
